topic_name: Types of Sentences and Interchange of Sentences

questions.question: Identify the sentence type: 'How wonderful the weather is!'
questions.explanation: Sentences expressing strong emotion ending with an exclamation mark are Exclamatory.

questions.question: Identify the sentence type: 'Please lend me your notebook.'
questions.explanation: Sentences expressing requests, commands, or advice are Imperative.

questions.question: Identify the sentence type: 'The Earth revolves around the sun.'
questions.explanation: Sentences making a factual statement or assertion are Assertive/Declarative.

questions.question: Identify the clause structure: 'Though he was poor, he was honest.'
questions.explanation: A sentence containing one principal clause and one subordinate clause (with 'Though') is a Complex sentence.

questions.question: Identify the clause structure: 'He worked hard and passed the examination.'
questions.explanation: Two independent coordinate clauses joined by coordinating conjunction 'and' form a Compound sentence.

questions.question: Identify the clause structure: 'In spite of his poverty, he was honest.'
questions.explanation: A sentence with only one finite verb ('was') and a prepositional phrase is a Simple sentence.

questions.question: Convert into Negative: 'As soon as he saw the police, he ran away.'
options: No sooner did he see the police than he ran away.
He saw the police and he did not run away.
No sooner had he saw the police when he ran away.
Hardly did he see the police than he ran away.
questions.explanation: Affirmative 'As soon as...' changes to negative 'No sooner did... than...'.

questions.question: Convert into Affirmative: 'Nobody was absent today.'
questions.explanation: 'Nobody was absent' is affirmatively equivalent to 'Everybody was present'.

questions.question: Convert into Assertive: 'Who does not love his country?'
questions.explanation: A negative rhetorical question 'Who does not love...?' transforms to affirmative assertive 'Everyone loves...'.

questions.question: Convert into Assertive: 'Can a man change his skin?'
options: A man cannot change his skin.
Man is able to change his skin.
A man can change his skin.
questions.explanation: Affirmative rhetorical question transforms into a negative assertive statement.

questions.question: Convert into Exclamatory: 'It is a very beautiful night.'
options: What a beautiful night it is!
How a beautiful night it is!
questions.explanation: Assertive with 'a very [adj] [noun]' transforms into 'What a [adj] [noun] it is!'

questions.question: Convert into Exclamatory: 'I wish I were a bird.'
options: O that I were a bird!
How I wish to be a bird!
questions.explanation: 'I wish I were...' transforms into exclamatory 'O that I were a bird!' or 'If only I were a bird!'

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'He finished his work and went home.'
options: Having finished his work, he went home.
After he had finished his work he went home.
He finished his work so he went home.
When he finished work he went home.
questions.explanation: Compound joined by 'and' reduces to Simple by using a participle phrase ('Having finished...').

questions.question: Convert into Compound: 'Besides being a poet, he was a philosopher.'
options: He was not only a poet but also a philosopher.
Though he was a poet he was a philosopher.
If he was a poet he was a philosopher.
He was a poet because he was a philosopher.
questions.explanation: 'Besides being...' converts to Compound using 'not only... but also...'.

questions.question: Convert into Complex: 'I saw a wounded bird.'
options: Seeing a wounded bird I stopped.
A wounded bird was seen by me.
I saw a bird which was wounded.
I saw a bird and it was wounded.
questions.explanation: Expanding the adjective 'wounded' into an adjective relative clause 'which was wounded' makes it Complex.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'He is too weak to walk.'
options: He cannot walk because of weak.
He is so weak that he cannot walk.
He is too weak that he can walk.
He is very weak and he cannot walk.
questions.explanation: 'too... to' transforms into 'so... that... cannot'.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'She is always on time.'
questions.explanation: Affirmative with antonym: 'always on time' becomes 'never late'.

questions.question: Transform into Affirmative: 'There is no smoke without fire.'
options: Where there is smoke, there is fire.
questions.explanation: Proverbial transformation: 'Where there is smoke, there is fire.'

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'Only a millionaire can afford this car.'
options: No one can afford this car except millionaire.
Only nobody can afford this car.
A millionaire only cannot afford this car.
None but a millionaire can afford this car.
questions.explanation: 'Only' applied to a person transforms to 'None but' in negative sentences.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'Only courage can save us.'
options: None but courage can save us.
Nothing but courage can save us.
questions.explanation: 'Only' applied to an abstract thing or non-person transforms to 'Nothing but'.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'Every mother loves her child.'
options: There is no mother but loves her child.
Every mother does not love child.
questions.explanation: 'Every [noun]' transforms into 'There is no [noun] but + verb...'

questions.question: Convert into Assertive: 'What though the field be lost?'
options: It does not matter much though the field be lost.
Though the field is lost we won.
questions.explanation: 'What though...' transforms to 'It does not matter much though...'

questions.question: Convert into Assertive: 'When can their glory fade?'
questions.explanation: Rhetorical question 'When can...?' transforms into '... can never fade.'

questions.question: Convert into Interrogative: 'Nobody can bear such an insult.'
options: Can anybody bear such an insult?
Cannot anybody bear such an insult?
questions.explanation: Negative statement transforms into affirmative question 'Can anybody bear...?'

questions.question: Convert into Interrogative: 'Money cannot buy happiness.'
questions.explanation: Negative statement transforms into positive interrogative 'Can money buy happiness?'

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Do or die.'
questions.explanation: Two imperative coordinate clauses connected by coordinating conjunction 'or'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Speak the truth and you will be respected.'
questions.explanation: Two coordinate clauses joined by 'and' -> Compound sentence.

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'He admitted that he was guilty.'
options: He was guilty and he admitted it.
Guilty as he was, he admitted.
Admitting that he was guilty he wept.
questions.explanation: Noun clause 'that he was guilty' is reduced to noun phrase 'his guilt' in a Simple sentence.

questions.question: Convert into Complex: 'He promised to help me.'
options: He promised that he would help me.
Promising to help me he left.
questions.explanation: Infinitive phrase 'to help me' expands into noun clause 'that he would help me'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Tell me where you live.'
questions.explanation: Principal clause 'Tell me' + noun clause 'where you live' = Complex sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Man proposes, but God disposes.'
questions.explanation: Coordinate clauses connected by adversative conjunction 'but' = Compound sentence.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'Brutus loved Caesar.'
options: Brutus was not without love for Caesar.
Brutus did not hate Caesar completely.
Brutus was without love for Caesar.
questions.explanation: Affirmative to negative without changing meaning: 'was not without love for Caesar'.

questions.question: Transform into Assertive: 'O that I had wings like a dove!'
options: How I have wings like dove!
I have wings like a dove.
I wish that I had wings like a dove.
questions.explanation: Exclamatory wish 'O that...' transforms to 'I wish that...'

questions.question: Transform into Exclamatory: 'It was a very tragic accident.'
options: What a tragic accident it was!
questions.explanation: 'What a tragic accident it was!'

questions.question: Convert into Compound: 'Owing to illness, he could not attend school.'
options: He was ill, therefore he could not attend school.
Because he was ill he could not attend school.
Being ill, he could not attend school.
Though he was ill, he attended school.
questions.explanation: Prepositional cause 'Owing to illness' becomes coordinate clause with 'therefore/so' in Compound.

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'He is rich, yet he is unhappy.'
options: Although he is rich, he is unhappy.
Rich as he is, he is unhappy.
In spite of being rich, he is unhappy.
questions.explanation: Adversative compound becomes Simple with 'In spite of being rich'.

questions.question: Convert into Complex: 'Search his pockets to find the key.'
options: Find the key by searching his pockets.
Searching his pockets he found the key.
Search his pockets and find the key.
Search his pockets so that you may find the key.
questions.explanation: Adverbial clause of purpose 'so that you may find the key' makes it Complex.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Unless you work hard, you will not succeed.'
questions.explanation: Subordinate clause of condition 'Unless you work hard' makes it a Complex sentence.

questions.question: Convert into Affirmative: 'No one could deny that he was clever.'
options: No one admitted that he was clever.
He was not clever to everyone.
Everyone had to admit that he was clever.
questions.explanation: 'No one could deny' -> 'Everyone had to admit'.

questions.question: Convert into Negative: 'He is always careful.'
questions.explanation: Affirmative -> 'never careless'.

questions.question: Transform into Assertive: 'If only I could see my mother once more!'
options: I might see my mother once more.
My mother wants to see me.
I strongly desire to see my mother once more.
Could I see my mother once more?
questions.explanation: 'If only I could...' transforms to assertive expression of strong desire.

questions.question: Convert into Interrogative: 'Everyone wishes to be happy.'
options: Does anyone wish to be happy?
Why does everyone wish to be happy?
Who does not wish to be happy?
questions.explanation: 'Everyone wishes...' transforms to rhetorical 'Who does not wish to be happy?'

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Get out of the room.'
questions.explanation: Direct command with implied subject 'You' is an Imperative sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'May you live happily!'
questions.explanation: Sentence expressing a prayer, wish, or blessing is an Optative sentence.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'She is richer than her sister.'
options: Her sister is as rich as she is.
Her sister is richer than she.
She is not as rich as her sister.
Her sister is not as rich as she is.
questions.explanation: Comparative to negative positive degree: 'Her sister is not as rich as she is.'

questions.question: Transform into Comparative: 'No other boy is as clever as Ramu.'
options: Ramu is not cleverer than any boy.
Any other boy is cleverer than Ramu.
Ramu is cleverer than any other boy.
questions.explanation: Positive to comparative: 'cleverer than any other boy'.

questions.question: Transform into Superlative: 'Iron is more useful than any other metal.'
options: Iron is useful of all metals.
No metal is most useful as iron.
Iron is the most useful of all metals.
Iron is the more useful metal.
questions.explanation: Comparative to superlative: 'the most useful of all metals'.

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'When the sun rose, the fog disappeared.'
options: As the sun rose the fog disappeared.
At sunrise the fog did not disappear.
The sun having risen, the fog disappeared.
The sun rose and the fog disappeared.
questions.explanation: Nominative absolute construction: 'The sun having risen, the fog disappeared.'

questions.question: Convert into Compound: 'If you do not run fast, you will miss the train.'
options: Unless you run fast you will miss the train.
Running fast or miss the train.
Running fast you will catch the train.
Run fast, or you will miss the train.
questions.explanation: Conditional complex clause transforms to alternative coordinate with 'or'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'The boy who won the prize is my nephew.'
questions.explanation: Relative clause 'who won the prize' modifying 'The boy' makes it a Complex sentence.

questions.question: Convert into Affirmative: 'She did not leave any stone unturned.'
options: She did not try every means.
questions.explanation: Idiomatic transformation: 'left no stone unturned' -> 'tried every possible means'.

questions.question: Convert into Negative: 'I shall always remember your help.'
options: I shall always not forget your help.
I shall not always remember your help.
I shall never forget your help.
I shall never remember your help.
questions.explanation: 'always remember' -> 'never forget'.

questions.question: Transform into Assertive: 'Who can touch pitch without being defiled?'
options: Anyone can touch pitch without being defiled.
No one can touch pitch without being defiled.
questions.explanation: Proverbial rhetorical question transforms to universal negative 'No one can...'

questions.question: Convert into Exclamatory: 'The sunset looks exceedingly lovely.'
options: What a lovely the sunset looks!
questions.explanation: 'How lovely the sunset looks!'

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'He worked hard so that he might pass.'
options: He passed because he worked hard.
questions.explanation: Adverbial purpose clause 'so that he might pass' reduces to infinitive of purpose 'to pass'.

questions.question: Convert into Compound: 'Hearing the noise, the child woke up.'
options: The child woke up because of noise.
As the child heard noise it woke up.
When the child heard the noise it woke up.
The child heard the noise and woke up.
questions.explanation: Participle simple sentence expands into coordinate clauses with 'and'.

questions.question: Convert into Complex: 'I know his residence.'
options: I know his house and residence.
questions.explanation: Noun phrase 'his residence' expands into noun clause 'where he lives'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'He confessed his crime.'
questions.explanation: Single subject 'He' and finite verb 'confessed' with object 'his crime' = Simple sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'He confessed that he had committed a crime.'
questions.explanation: Main clause + noun clause 'that he had committed a crime' = Complex sentence.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'All must die.'
questions.explanation: Philosophical affirmative transforms to 'None can escape death.'

questions.question: Transform into Affirmative: 'None but the brave deserve the fair.'
options: Only the brave deserve the fair.
questions.explanation: 'None but' transforms to affirmative 'Only'.

questions.question: Transform into Assertive: 'What a piece of work is man!'
options: Man is a wonderful piece of work.
Man is not a piece of work.
What man is a piece of work!
Is man a piece of work?
questions.explanation: Shakespearean exclamation transforms to assertive statement.

questions.question: Convert into Interrogative: 'Their bravery cannot be questioned.'
options: Why can their bravery be questioned?
questions.explanation: Negative assertive statement -> affirmative question 'Can their bravery be questioned?'

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'He is so old that he cannot run.'
options: He is very old and cannot run.
He cannot run because he is old.
He is too old to run.
questions.explanation: 'so... that... cannot' reduces to 'too... to'.

questions.question: Convert into Compound: 'In addition to giving him advice, I gave him money.'
options: Giving him advice I gave him money.
I gave him not only advice but also money.
I gave advice because I gave money.
Though I gave advice I gave money.
questions.explanation: Cumulative addition transforms to 'not only... but also...' in a Compound sentence.

questions.question: Convert into Complex: 'I saw a blind man.'
options: Seeing a blind man I stopped.
I saw a man and he was blind.
A blind man was seen by me.
I saw a man who was blind.
questions.explanation: Adjective 'blind' expands to relative clause 'who was blind'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be.'
questions.explanation: Correlative coordinating conjunction 'neither... nor' connects coordinate imperative elements = Compound.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'God made the country and man made the town.'
questions.explanation: Two coordinate clauses joined by 'and' = Compound sentence.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'As soon as the bell rang, the boys entered the class.'
options: The bell rang and no sooner boys entered.
No sooner had the bell rang when the boys entered.
No sooner did the bell ring than the boys entered the class.
Hardly did the bell ring when the boys entered.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as...' -> 'No sooner did [V1]... than...'

questions.question: Transform into Affirmative: 'I am not a little surprised.'
questions.explanation: 'Not a little' means 'greatly/very much'.

questions.question: Transform into Assertive: 'Could I ever forget those happy days?'
options: Could I forget those days never?
I could forget those happy days.
I could never forget those happy days.
questions.explanation: Rhetorical question -> 'I could never forget...'

questions.question: Convert into Exclamatory: 'I wish that I were young again.'
options: What a young man I am!
O for a youth once again!
questions.explanation: Poetic wish transforms to 'O for...' or 'If only I were young again!'

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'We eat so that we may live.'
questions.explanation: 'so that we may live' reduces to infinitive 'to live'.

questions.question: Convert into Compound: 'Besides being punished, he was fined.'
options: Though he was punished he was fined.
He was not only punished but also fined.
He was punished because he was fined.
questions.explanation: 'Besides being...' -> 'He was not only punished but also fined.'

questions.question: Convert into Complex: 'He told me the time of his arrival.'
options: He told me about his arrival time.
He arrived and told me the time.
He told me when he would arrive.
Telling me the time he arrived.
questions.explanation: Noun phrase 'the time of his arrival' expands to noun clause 'when he would arrive'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Wait until I return.'
questions.explanation: Main imperative clause + subordinate time clause 'until I return' = Complex sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Listen carefully and take notes.'
questions.explanation: Two coordinate imperative clauses joined by 'and' = Compound sentence.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'Every rose has a thorn.'
options: Every rose does not have thorn.
There is no rose without a thorn.
questions.explanation: Universal truth transforms to 'There is no rose without a thorn.'

questions.question: Transform into Affirmative: 'He did not leave me alone.'
questions.explanation: Negative -> 'He kept me company'.

questions.question: Transform into Assertive: 'Who would not like to be rich?'
options: Nobody would like to be rich.
Would anyone like to be rich?
Everyone would like to be rich.
questions.explanation: Rhetorical question -> 'Everyone would like to be rich.'

questions.question: Convert into Exclamatory: 'It was a terrible storm.'
options: What a terrible storm it was!
questions.explanation: 'What a terrible storm it was!'

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'A man who is industrious is sure to succeed.'
options: An industrious man will succeed and be sure.
Being industrious a man is sure to succeed.
An industrious man is sure to succeed.
If a man is industrious he succeeds.
questions.explanation: Adjective clause 'who is industrious' reduces to single attributive adjective 'industrious'.

questions.question: Convert into Compound: 'He took his gun and shot the tiger.'
options: Having taken his gun, he shot the tiger (Simple form).
He took his gun and shot the tiger.
Taking his gun he shot tiger.
When he took gun he shot tiger.
questions.explanation: The sentence 'He took his gun and shot the tiger' is already a Compound sentence joined by 'and'.

questions.question: Convert into Complex: 'I heard of his failure.'
options: He failed and I heard it.
Hearing of his failure I felt sad.
I heard that he had failed.
questions.explanation: Noun phrase 'his failure' expands into noun clause 'that he had failed'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Although the weather was bad, the plane took off.'
questions.explanation: 'Although...' introduces an adverbial concession clause -> Complex sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'The sun set and night fell.'
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'and' = Compound sentence.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'He is the best boy in the class.'
options: Other boys are not better than he.
He is not the worst boy in the class.
No other boy in the class is as good as he is.
No boy is good as he.
questions.explanation: Superlative transforms to negative positive degree: 'No other boy... is as good as he is.'

questions.question: Transform into Affirmative: 'Nobody denied the fact.'
questions.explanation: 'Nobody denied' -> 'Everybody accepted'.

questions.question: Transform into Assertive: 'What is the use of crying over split milk?'
options: It is of no use crying over spilt milk.
Can we cry over spilt milk?
There is use of crying over spilt milk.
questions.explanation: Rhetorical question -> 'It is of no use crying over spilt milk.'

questions.question: Convert into Exclamatory: 'You have grown very tall.'
questions.explanation: 'How tall you have grown!'

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'He failed in the exam, which surprised us.'
options: His failure in the exam surprised us.
When he failed it surprised us.
He failed in exam and it surprised us.
Because he failed it surprised us.
questions.explanation: Complex relative clause reduces to noun phrase subject 'His failure in the exam surprised us.'

questions.question: Convert into Compound: 'Walk fast lest you should miss the bus.'
options: If you don't walk fast you miss bus.
Walk fast, otherwise you will miss the bus.
questions.explanation: 'lest... should' transforms to Compound with 'otherwise' or 'or'.

questions.question: Convert into Complex: 'The time of his departure is unknown.'
options: When he will depart is unknown.
He will depart and time is unknown.
questions.explanation: Noun phrase expands into noun clause subject 'When he will depart is unknown.'

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Since you are here, help me with this.'
questions.explanation: Subordinate clause of reason 'Since you are here' + imperative main clause = Complex sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Work hard, or you will fail.'
questions.explanation: Coordinate clauses connected by alternative conjunction 'or' = Compound sentence.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'She is too proud to beg.'
options: She is proud so she begs.
She cannot beg because of pride.
She is very proud and she will not beg.
She is so proud that she will not beg.
questions.explanation: 'too... to' -> 'so proud that she will not beg'.

questions.question: Transform into Affirmative: 'I am not uncertain of his success.'
options: I am doubtful of his success.
I am not sure of his success.
I am certain of his success.
His success is uncertain to me.
questions.explanation: Double negative 'not uncertain' -> affirmative 'certain'.

questions.question: Transform into Assertive: 'Is this the way to behave?'
options: This is the way to behave.
Can this be the way to behave?
This is not the way to behave.
questions.explanation: Affirmative rhetorical question -> negative assertive statement 'This is not the way to behave.'

questions.question: Convert into Exclamatory: 'I earnestly wish to see my homeland again.'
options: O to see my homeland again!
questions.explanation: Intense wish transforms to exclamatory infinitive 'O to see my homeland again!'

questions.question: Convert into Simple: 'The teacher entered the room and all stood up.'
options: On the teacher entering the room, all stood up.
The teacher having entered the room all stood up.
When teacher entered all stood up.
As teacher entered room all stood up.
questions.explanation: Nominative absolute construction 'The teacher having entered the room, all stood up.'

questions.question: Convert into Compound: 'Not only did he give me advice, but he also helped me financially.'
options: He helped me because he gave advice.
He gave me advice and he helped me financially as well.
Though he gave advice he helped me.
questions.explanation: 'Not only... but also' is a correlative compound coordinator.

questions.question: Convert into Complex: 'He was punished for his disobedience.'
options: He was disobedient and so he was punished.
He was punished because he was disobedient.
questions.explanation: Prepositional cause 'for his disobedience' expands into adverbial clause of cause 'because he was disobedient'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Neither John nor his brother attended the meeting.'
questions.explanation: Only one finite verb ('attended') with compound subject = Simple sentence!

questions.question: Identify the type: 'He tried hard, yet he could not succeed.'
questions.explanation: Adversative coordinating conjunction 'yet' connects two coordinate clauses = Compound sentence.

questions.question: Transform into Negative: 'Where there is love, there is peace.'
options: There is no peace where there is love.
There is no love without peace.
Love and peace do not exist.
questions.explanation: Affirmative proverb transforms into 'There is no love without peace.'

questions.question: Convert to Negative: 'He is always punctual.'
questions.explanation: Affirmative with antonym: 'always punctual' becomes 'never late'.

questions.question: Convert to Simple: 'He must work hard, or he will not pass.'
options: He must work hard to pass.
If he does not work hard he fails.
Working hard he will not pass.
questions.explanation: Compound clause with 'or' reduces to simple with infinitive of purpose 'to pass'.

questions.question: Convert to Complex: 'I saw a running deer.'
options: I saw a deer which was running.
A running deer was seen by me.
Seeing a deer it was running.
I saw a deer and it was running.
questions.explanation: Adjective participle 'running' expands into relative clause 'which was running'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Tell me the truth or leave the room.'
questions.explanation: Two coordinate imperative clauses connected by 'or' = Compound.

questions.question: Convert to Assertive: 'What a terrible tragedy!'
options: It was a very terrible tragedy.
It is not a terrible tragedy.
questions.explanation: Exclamatory statement transforms to assertive declarative.

questions.question: Convert to Affirmative: 'No one will dispute your integrity.'
questions.explanation: 'No one will dispute' -> 'Everyone will acknowledge'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'He returned home because he was unwell.'
questions.explanation: Subordinate clause of reason introduced by 'because' = Complex sentence.

questions.question: Convert to Simple: 'The thief saw the policeman and fled.'
options: Seeing the policeman, the thief fled.
When the thief saw policeman he fled.
The policeman saw thief and fled.
The thief saw policeman so he fled.
questions.explanation: Compound sentence reduces to simple via participle 'Seeing the policeman'.

questions.question: Convert to Compound: 'In spite of the heavy rain, the match continued.'
options: It rained heavily, yet the match continued.
Although it rained the match continued.
questions.explanation: Prepositional concession transforms to coordinate clause with 'yet'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Barking dogs seldom bite.'
questions.explanation: Single subject and single finite verb ('bite') = Simple sentence.

questions.question: Convert to Interrogative: 'Nobody can escape destiny.'
questions.explanation: Negative statement transforms to affirmative question 'Can anybody escape destiny?'

questions.question: Convert to Assertive: 'Shall I ever forget your kindness?'
options: I shall never forget your kindness.
questions.explanation: Rhetorical question transforms to 'I shall never forget your kindness.'

questions.question: Convert to Exclamatory: 'The sunset looks very splendid.'
options: What a splendid the sunset looks!
questions.explanation: 'How splendid the sunset looks!'

questions.question: Convert to Negative: 'Only graduates need apply.'
questions.explanation: 'Only' applied to persons transforms to 'None but' in negative.

questions.question: Convert to Affirmative: 'He did not fail to notice the change.'
options: He failed to notice the change.
questions.explanation: Double negative 'did not fail to notice' = 'noticed'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'If you sow good seeds, you will reap a good harvest.'
questions.explanation: Subordinate conditional clause + main clause = Complex sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'The sun rose and the birds began to sing.'
questions.explanation: Two coordinate independent clauses joined by 'and' = Compound sentence.

questions.question: Convert to Simple: 'He bought a house that belonged to his uncle.'
options: He bought house and it belonged to uncle.
Belonging to uncle he bought house.
questions.explanation: Relative clause reduces to possessive noun phrase 'his uncle's house'.

questions.question: Convert to Compound: 'Besides being clever, he is hardworking.'
options: He is not only clever but also hardworking.
Though he is clever he is hardworking.
Because he is clever he works hard.
questions.explanation: 'Besides being...' -> 'not only... but also...'

questions.question: Convert to Complex: 'He declared his innocence.'
options: He declared and he was innocent.
He declared that he was innocent.
questions.explanation: Noun phrase 'his innocence' expands into noun clause 'that he was innocent'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'May God grant you peace and happiness!'
questions.explanation: Sentence expressing a blessing or prayer is Optative.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Don't lean against the wet paint.'
questions.explanation: Command/warning addressed to implied 'You' is Imperative.

questions.question: Convert to Negative: 'All men are mortal.'
questions.explanation: Affirmative universal transforms to 'No man is immortal.'

questions.question: Convert to Affirmative: 'There is nobody who does not love freedom.'
questions.explanation: Double negative transforms to 'Everybody loves freedom.'

questions.question: Convert to Assertive: 'Who does not know Mahatma Gandhi?'
questions.explanation: Rhetorical question transforms to 'Everyone knows Mahatma Gandhi.'

questions.question: Convert to Interrogative: 'Their sacrifice will never be forgotten.'
options: Will not their sacrifice be forgotten?
Will their sacrifice ever be forgotten?
questions.explanation: Negative statement transforms to positive question with 'ever'.

questions.question: Convert to Exclamatory: 'I wish I had met him earlier.'
options: If only I had met him earlier!
questions.explanation: 'I wish I had...' transforms to 'If only I had...'

questions.question: Convert to Simple: 'As soon as he got the telegram, he left.'
options: When he got telegram he left.
Immediately on getting the telegram, he left.
questions.explanation: Subordinate time clause reduces to prepositional phrase 'Immediately on getting...'

questions.question: Convert to Compound: 'Though he was wealthy, he lived a simple life.'
options: He was wealthy, yet he lived a simple life.
In spite of wealth he lived simple.
Because he was wealthy he lived simple.
questions.explanation: Complex clause of concession transforms to compound with 'yet'.

questions.question: Convert to Complex: 'A rolling stone gathers no moss.'
options: A stone which rolls gathers no moss.
A stone rolls and gathers no moss.
Stone gathers no moss when rolling.
questions.explanation: Participle adjective 'rolling' expands into relative clause 'which rolls'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Speak clearly so that everyone can hear you.'
questions.explanation: Adverbial clause of purpose 'so that everyone can hear you' = Complex.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'He was tired; therefore, he went to bed early.'
questions.explanation: Two coordinate clauses joined by illative conjunction 'therefore' = Compound.

questions.question: Convert to Negative: 'She is too weak to walk alone.'
options: She cannot walk alone because of weak.
She is very weak and cannot walk alone.
She is so weak that she cannot walk alone.
She is weak so she walks alone.
questions.explanation: 'too... to' -> 'so... that... cannot'.

questions.question: Convert to Affirmative: 'None but the pure in heart shall see God.'
options: The pure in heart never see God.
All pure in heart shall see God.
Only the pure in heart shall see God.
questions.explanation: 'None but' transforms to 'Only'.

questions.question: Convert to Assertive: 'How sweet the moonlight sleeps upon this bank!'
options: The moonlight sleeps very sweetly upon this bank.
questions.explanation: Shakespearean exclamation transforms into assertive statement.

questions.question: Convert to Interrogative: 'It is useless to offer help to an ungrateful person.'
options: Can anyone help an ungrateful person?
Is it useless to help anyone?
What is the use of offering help to an ungrateful person?
questions.explanation: 'It is useless to...' transforms to rhetorical question 'What is the use of...?'

questions.question: Convert to Exclamatory: 'It is a terribly cold morning.'
options: What a cold morning is it!
questions.explanation: 'How cold the morning is!'

questions.question: Convert to Simple: 'He ran fast so that he might catch the train.'
options: Because he ran fast he caught train.
He ran fast to catch the train.
He ran fast and caught the train.
questions.explanation: Purpose clause reduces to infinitive 'to catch the train'.

questions.question: Convert to Compound: 'Owing to heavy fog, all flights were delayed.'
options: There was heavy fog, and so all flights were delayed.
Because there was fog flights delayed.
In spite of fog flights delayed.
questions.explanation: Cause phrase expands into coordinate clause joined by 'and so'.

questions.question: Convert to Complex: 'He admitted his fault.'
options: He admitted that he had made a fault.
He had a fault and admitted it.
His fault was admitted by him.
questions.explanation: Noun phrase expands into noun clause 'that he had made a fault'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Neither John nor his sister came to school today.'
questions.explanation: Single finite verb ('came') with compound subject = Simple sentence.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Work carefully, otherwise you will make errors.'
questions.explanation: Coordinate clauses connected by alternative conjunction 'otherwise' = Compound.

questions.question: Convert to Negative: 'Every cloud has a silver lining.'
options: There is no cloud without a silver lining.
Every cloud does not have silver lining.
No cloud has a silver lining.
questions.explanation: Proverbial transformation: 'There is no cloud without a silver lining.'

questions.question: Convert to Affirmative: 'I cannot but admire his dedication.'
options: I do not admire his dedication.
questions.explanation: 'cannot but + V1' = 'must + V1'.

questions.question: Convert to Assertive: 'What though we lose the game?'
options: We lost the game and it matters.
It matters little though we lose the game.
questions.explanation: 'What though...' transforms to 'It matters little though...'

questions.question: Convert to Interrogative: 'Everyone appreciates honesty.'
questions.explanation: Universal affirmative transforms to rhetorical question 'Who does not appreciate honesty?'

questions.question: Convert to Simple: 'A man who is honest is respected by all.'
options: A man is honest and respected.
An honest man is respected by all.
Being honest a man is respected.
If a man is honest he is respected.
questions.explanation: Relative clause reduces to attributive adjective 'An honest man'.

questions.question: Convert to Compound: 'To everyone's surprise, the underdog won.'
options: Because the underdog won everyone surprised.
The underdog won, and this surprised everyone.
questions.explanation: Prepositional phrase expands to coordinate clause with 'and'.

questions.question: Convert to Complex: 'I heard of his great success.'
options: Hearing of his success I cheered.
I heard that he had succeeded greatly.
He succeeded and I heard it.
His success was heard by me.
questions.explanation: Noun phrase expands to noun clause 'that he had succeeded greatly'.

questions.question: Identify the type: 'Unless you hurry, you will miss the morning bus.'
questions.explanation: Conditional subordinate clause introduced by 'Unless' = Complex.
